startup.name: Axonnic
startup.one_liner: Creating human skill at robot scale
startup.description: Axonnic builds wearable EMG sensors that capture human muscle activity, effort and force while people demonstrate physical tasks, to sell as training data for dexterous robot learning. Customers are robotics labs and humanoid companies. Two founders, San Francisco and remote, Fall 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is known to have been accepted, so this is a placeholder note and not a real estimate. The prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md), and this team would sit near the middle to upper end given the hot physical AI theme within that range.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. If YC had said no, the likely reasons would be that EMG signals may add little over video and tactile data, the customer base of robotics labs is small and unproven, and similar companies are already in the batch pool.

narrative.headline: A novel but unproven data layer for robots that probably reaches a small seed.
narrative.general_summary: Axonnic is a two person team building wearable EMG sensors to collect human skill data for robot learning. Physical AI is a hot theme and Industrials companies reach seed fast, so a seed above $500K is likely but not certain. The core risk is whether EMG adds value over video, tactile and teleoperation data, and the customer base of robotics labs is small. Similar YC companies such as Relari and Sensei had no priced rounds in the data, and later rounds depend on a clear lift in robot performance. A pivot toward robotics products or human computer interaction is a possible upside.
